glyphs.notes: Use a five-column shared body derived from the paired native a/turned-a cap and stave entrances, with two equal six-pixel counters and a compact two-row waist. The left shoulder enters below its crest; the right hip leaves above the baseline. Joined staves retain simple native n/m/u endings. Middle components follow allocation order from left to right; only their designated upper or lower extension pixels change between states. Outer curved terminals use the approved dense-family hook and simple eng return; no extra tip, serif, or enclosed terminal pocket is added. This allocation contains no declared long bowl or returnContact, so ordinary compact hooks are not forced to close against unrelated staves.

glyphs.notes: Use a five-column shared body derived from the paired native a/turned-a cap and stave entrances, with two equal six-pixel counters and a compact two-row waist. The left shoulder enters below its crest; the right hip leaves above the baseline. Joined staves retain simple native n/m/u endings. Middle components follow allocation order from left to right; only their designated upper or lower extension pixels change between states. Outer curved terminals use the approved dense-family hook and simple eng return; no extra tip, serif, or enclosed terminal pocket is added. This allocation contains no declared long bowl or returnContact, so ordinary compact hooks are not forced to close against unrelated staves. The listed outer-stave joining pixels continue straight extensions through a rounded native cap or return.

glyphs.notes: Use a five-column shared body derived from the paired native a/turned-a cap and stave entrances, with two equal six-pixel counters and a compact two-row waist. The left shoulder enters below its crest; the right hip leaves above the baseline. Joined staves retain simple native n/m/u endings. Middle components follow allocation order from left to right; only their designated upper or lower extension pixels change between states. Outer curved terminals use the approved dense-family hook and simple eng return; no extra tip, serif, or enclosed terminal pocket is added. This allocation contains no declared long bowl or returnContact, so ordinary compact hooks are not forced to close against unrelated staves.

glyphs.notes: The turned arches are drawn on the unchanged Latin body rows, following native turned m and u hips, rather than rotating the entire 16-row cell. The long left bowl occupies columns 1 through 3 from row 3 to row 13. Its one-pixel open return is at (3,5), immediately above the adjacent first middle arm. Extending that arm fills the opening; extending the farther arm at column 5 leaves it open. Compound ascenders use the unadorned vertical terminals of native h and q, avoiding head-serifs that would bridge neighboring staves. State: neither middle component extended.
reviewNotes: The left-only and both states close exactly the same long bowl; the right-only state leaves the opening at (3,5) unchanged.
The first extension overlaps the pre-existing returning terminal at (3,4), so its visible difference adds two pixels, (3,3) and (3,5).
The extended right outer stem reaches rows 3 and 15 without gaining a broad dotless-i foot.
